Practical 4

Embedding Ocean Products in your website

Four ways to put content from another website on a web page: fetch data and draw a chart, show a finished picture, embed a PDF, or embed a whole web page.

Tide Gauge

Loading...

// Packages used: chart.js       install it once with:  npm install chart.js
import Chart from 'chart.js/auto'

// fetch is built into every browser, so nothing to install for that part.
// The data arrives as JSON, so we fetch it and pick the parts we need.

// 1. Ask the API, and read the reply as JSON
const response = await fetch('https://ocean-obs-api.spc.int/insitu/get_data/station/fong?limit=1000')
const result = await response.json()

// 2. Sort oldest first, so the line reads left to right in time
const records = result.data.slice().sort((a, b) => a.time < b.time ? -1 : 1)

// 3. Throw away error readings (tide gauges mark these as -999)
const good = records.filter(r => r['sea_level (m)'] !== Number(result.bad_data))

// 4. Split into x axis labels and y axis values
const labels = good.map(r => r.time.slice(0, 16).replace('T', ' '))
const values = good.map(r => r['sea_level (m)'])

// 5. Hand both lists to Chart.js, which does the drawing
new Chart(document.getElementById('tide-chart'), {
  type: 'line',
  data: {
    labels: labels,
    datasets: [{ label: 'Sea level (m)', data: values, borderColor: '#2a78d6' }]
  }
})

Ocean Map

Loading...

// Packages used: none. Plain HTML and JavaScript, nothing to install.

// There is no fetch here either. The plotter has already drawn the map, so we are
// given a finished picture - setting src makes the browser download it.

const image = document.getElementById('ocean-map')

// The load event tells us the picture has arrived
image.onload = () => {
  status.textContent = 'Image loaded from the plotter service.'
}

// If the URL is wrong the picture never arrives, so say so
image.onerror = () => {
  status.textContent = 'Could not load that image. Check the URL.'
}

// Setting src last means the two handlers above are ready before it loads
image.src = 'https://ocean-plotter.spc.int/plotter/getMap?region=6&layer_map=5'
          + '&time=2026-08-02T00:00:00Z&unit=metric&use_cache=True&token=null'

Tide Calendar

Open the tide calendar in a new tab

Loading...

// Packages used: none. Every browser already has a built-in PDF viewer.

<!-- A PDF is not fetched or parsed either. We only say where it lives,
     twice, and let the browser's own PDF viewer do the rest. -->

<!-- Way 1 - a link. target="_blank" opens it in a new browser tab.
     rel="noopener" is a safety habit whenever you use target="_blank". -->
<a href="calendar.pdf" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Open the tide calendar</a>

<!-- Way 2 - the same PDF inside our page. This is an iframe, not an img,
     because a PDF has pages to scroll rather than being one picture. -->
<iframe src="calendar.pdf" title="Tide calendar PDF"></iframe>


// In practical-4.js we only fill in the two addresses:
const url = 'https://ocean-library.spc.int/library/media/b4da9347d92b480e882f63fc583d680e_pdf.pdf'

document.getElementById('calendar-link').href = url   // Way 1
document.getElementById('calendar-pdf').src = url     // Way 2

// The button beside the link opens the same address itself
window.open(url, '_blank', 'noopener')

Ocean Portal Explorer

The same iframe that held the PDF can hold a whole web page - here the Ocean Portal explorer, still fully clickable. The long share= part of the address is the saved view.

Open the explorer in a new tab

Loading...

// Packages used: none. An iframe is part of HTML itself.

<!-- One tag is the whole trick. The other site loads and runs inside this
     box, keeping its own scrolling, buttons and map controls. -->
<iframe id="ocean-explorer" title="Pacific Ocean Portal explorer"></iframe>


// And in practical-4.js, the same one line as the PDF:
document.getElementById('ocean-explorer').src =
  'https://oceanportal.spc.int/explorer?share=N4IgNghgngpgTgZxALgNqgJYBMUGYA0408A...'

// Worth knowing: a site can refuse to be embedded. Sites send a header
// (X-Frame-Options or Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors) that tells
// the browser who may frame them, and the browser obeys it. If the box stays
// blank, that is usually why - not a mistake in your code. Always offer a
// plain link as well, as this tab does, so there is a way through.

Exercise 4 - Embed a whole web page

Below is the Bureau of Meteorology's printable tide table for Port Vila . Paste any page address, then press Show page.

  • aac=INT_TP027 and region=VUT - which station.
  • date=4-8-2026 and days=7 - the week to show.

If the box stays blank, that site has told the browser it will not be embedded. Use the link instead - it is not a fault in your page.
